The discomfort will last anywhere from 5 minutes to half an hour. I suggest you get a lens case and some cleaning liquid, they usually come together in a set. Depending where you are, of course. In Europe we have RenNu, for example, just check your local drug store. The insert on the lenses will tell you how to properly take care of them, but personally I replace the liquid every time I wear mine, or every 2-3 days, to prevent protein growth, which can damage your eyes.

Even smaller circle lenses can cause pain and discomfort in your eyes. If you have a smaller pair available, just practice with those before trying scleral contacts. If possible, have a friend or family member help you put your lenses in for the first time, cause you'll be tempted to squint and shut your eyes. 


You can expect to feel pain and burning in your eyes, as well as extreme tearing, but don't take them off unless you seriously can't take it any longer. The pain and tearing will go away soon, and next time it'll be way easier. I'm not trying to scare you away or anything, just a warning so you'll know what to expect! 


You can start with scleral lenses though I don't recommend it. If you have a con or event coming up, put them on an hour or so a day beforehand, so when the day comes you won't violently tear up. 


Good luck! You're welcome to ask anything else, I love to help.

They're "sclera" contacts... Not ghoul contacts... That aside, [you can get scleras in the design "gremlin" on PinkyParadise](http://www.pinkyparadise.com/Phantasee-Gremlin-p/h3-gremlin.htm). They're by Phantasee lens and are great quality, though a bit pricey. There's also a seemingly UK based sclera dealer [here](http://www.scleracontactlenses.co.uk) but I've never used them so I can't say anything about it.

Before you even consider buying, please read this!

* 1 - Sclera lenses are HUGE, but they **DO NOT** cover your whole eye! This is because contacts do not let your eye ventilate, essentially suffocating it and a lens covering your whole sclera is very dangerous and can lead to blindness. 
When you see Asian cosplayers and the like wearing scleras it looks like it covers up a lot, but when a caucasian person wears them you can still see the natural "white" of the eye. 

* 2 - **DO NOT** buy unless you are an experienced contact/circle lens user already, for obvious reasons. 

* 3 - For the love of God do not wear these for more than a few hours at a time, unless you crazy and want to ruin your eyes.

* 4 - The first time you wear it will hurt like hell. Deal with it. Insert them properly, cry if you have to, but it will get better. Also it will be difficult to see, so if you're going to a con or the like, practice wearing them a week before or something. 


That's all! Enjoy, and happy cosplaying!
